subject: science
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Name living and non-living things they see around them
Tell living things from non-living things by what can be observed
Sort things into living and non-living groups
Describe the features of living and non-living things in their own words
Draw living and non-living things and name them
Feel care and sensitivity towards plants, animals and the environment
Find and name the main internal organs on a picture, model or cut-out
Draw the major internal organs and label them
Name the parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) and what each does
Explain breathing in and breathing out in their own words, using a model
Explain why proper breathing and deep breathing are good for health
Name the causes of air pollution and suggest ways to reduce it, at an awareness level
Recognise and name common birds seen in their surroundings
Draw birds and label their body parts: beaks, feet and feathers
Group birds by beak, feather and claw types
Describe what some common birds eat, and how birds fly
Recognise the nests of some birds, such as the weaver, tailor and woodpecker
Make a model of a nest with local materials
Care for birds, for example by setting up a bird bath
Name common insects, such as ants, beetles, bees, flies, mosquitoes and butterflies
Label the body parts of an insect: head, thorax, abdomen, legs and wings
Explain the life cycle of a butterfly and of a honey bee in their own words
Name insects that harm people, and suggest ways to protect against them
Explain why social insects such as ants and bees are useful to people
Feel compassion for insects and other small creatures
Name the parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower and fruit) and say what each does
Name the parts of a seed and tell different kinds of seeds apart, such as gram and green pea
Know that germination needs water, air and warmth
Carry out a simple seed germination experiment with help from elders
Appreciate the beauty of plants, through leaves and flowers
Care for plants and their surroundings
Classify plants as herbs, shrubs, trees and climbers, with examples
Name the parts of plants we eat: leaves, roots, fruits, seeds and flowers
Name plant products such as oil, spices and pulses
Name some medicinal plants and the seeds, leaves or buds used from them
Draw and colour plants and fruits
Show respect for food and avoid wasting it

topics.topic: Forms of Matter: Solids, Liquids and Gases
covers: Tell natural things from man-made things in the surroundings
Identify solids, liquids and gases from what can be observed about them
Give examples of each form found at home and around them
Watch simple experiments that show the properties of each form, such as ice, water and vapour
Explain the uses of solids, liquids and gases in daily life
Observe some properties of water
Sort materials into those that dissolve in water and those that do not
Make simple solutions with salt and sugar
Find out which objects float and which sink
Notice that warm water and stirring help substances dissolve
Name the three forms of water: solid, liquid and gas
Explain the water cycle, including evaporation and condensation, in simple words
Draw the water cycle and label the forms of water in it
Name the common causes of water pollution
Describe simple ways to purify water at home or school
Explain rainwater harvesting and why it helps to conserve water
Describe the uses of the sun, such as drying and cooking
Explain how a solar cooker, a solar cell and a solar heater work, in simple terms
Explain that plants need sunlight to make their food
Explain why living things need the sun
Tell renewable and non-renewable sources of energy apart, with examples
Suggest ways to save energy at home and at school
Keep their own body clean: hands, nails, hair, teeth and clothes
Name the causes of unclean surroundings, such as polythene, spitting and garbage
List the do's and don'ts for keeping surroundings clean
Suggest ways to keep public places clean
Know what helps the body stay healthy: food, rest, exercise and play
Know about the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and small actions that help it

gaps: Causes, effects and prevention of air pollution are taught in depth in Class IV Social Studies, so Class III covers only awareness.
The curriculum does not name fixed bird or insect species; the teacher chooses the examples to suit the children.
